content.summary: Major aspects of management of patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guideline are summarized. The page provides an overview of levels of evidence, a central illustration (Figure 1), common abbreviations, and guidance on initial assessment and triage for suspected ACS.

level_of_evidence.A: Data derived from multiple randomized clinical trials or meta-analyses.
level_of_evidence.B: Data derived from a single randomized clinical trial or large non-randomized studies.
level_of_evidence.C: Consensus of opinion of the experts and/or small studies, retrospective studies, registries.

content.initial_assessment_and_triage: If ACS is suspected, perform initial triage and assessment including an electrocardiogram (ECG) to assess for abnormalities or evidence of ischaemia, targeted clinical history to assess context of presentation, and targeted clinical examination to assess clinical and haemodynamic stability. Based on initial assessment, decide whether immediate invasive management is required.
content.management_note: Patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) require primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) when indicated.
